doc.title: Phil Schaap interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003

title: First hearing Charlie Parker
summary: He first heard Parker on Night in Tunisia on a Dial 78 from Ross Russell.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Can you recall the first time you heard Charlie Parker?
I think the “Night in Tunisia” on Yellow Dial label when Ross Russell came to close up things in 1955, if it was ’55.
Yeah. Did it make a particular impression on you at the time?

I liked that one record. That’s the one that I pulled out of — the records that he gave me I kept aside and didn’t really get into until I was in junior high school. But a “Night in Tunisia” was in my regular stack. So there may be more Dizzy stories. But he’s not on the record. The trumpet player is Miles Davis. And it’s a 78 that tells you that he’s on the record, the personnel is on the label.
